chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Abī Ayyūb, from Ḍurays al-Kunāsī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman and a slave who killed a man by mistake. He said: “Indeed, the mistake of the woman and the slave is like intentional killing; so if the heirs of the slain wish to kill them both, they may kill them both.”

He said: “And if the value of the slave is more than five thousand dirhams, then they must return to his master whatever exceeds five thousand dirhams. And if they wish to kill the woman and take the slave, they may do so, unless his value is more than five thousand dirhams; then they must return to the master of the slave whatever exceeds five thousand dirhams and take the slave. Or his master may ransom him. And if the value of the slave is less than five thousand dirhams, then they have no claim except the slave.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءُ الْمَقْتُولِ: the heirs or legal claimants of the slain person
key_terms.الْعَبْدِ: the slave involved in the killing and subject to legal claim
key_terms.خَمْسَةِ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ: the legal financial threshold of five thousand dirhams mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.قِيمَةُ الْعَبْدِ: the assessed monetary value of the slave
key_terms.يَفْتَدِيَهُ: to ransom him; meaning the master redeems the slave by payment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman and a slave jointly kill someone by mistake in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning accidental killing committed jointly by a woman and a slave. It explains the options available to the heirs of the slain person, including retaliation, taking the slave, and financial adjustment based on the slave’s value, showing detailed judicial treatment of qiṣāṣ and compensation.
